sanskrit: tathā kalyāṇaśīlas tvaṃ brāhmaṇeṣu mahātmasu anāgāḥ sarvabhūteṣu karkaśatvam upeyivān
english: You who were thus of noble character toward the great-souled brahmins, blameless toward all beings, have now acquired harshness.

sanskrit: pratiṣiddho mayā tāta raibhyāvasathadarśanāt gatavān eva taṃ kṣudraṃ kālāntakayamopamam
english: Though forbidden by me, dear son, from visiting the dwelling of Raibhya, you went anyway to that vile one who is like Death and the end-time Yama.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa jānan mahātejā vṛddhasyaikaṃ mamātmajam gatavān eva kopasya vaśaṃ paramadurmatiḥ
english: That one of great splendor, knowing he was my only son, an old man's sole child, was entirely given over to anger — a man of utterly wicked mind.

sanskrit: putraśokam anuprāpya eṣa raibhyasya karmaṇā tyakṣyāmi tvām ṛte putra prāṇān iṣṭatamān bhuvi
english: Having been overtaken by grief over a son through this deed of Raibhya's, I shall abandon, except for you, my son, these most dear breaths of life in this world.

sanskrit: yathāhaṃ putraśokena dehaṃ tyakṣyāmi kilbiṣī tathā jyeṣṭhaḥ suto raibhyaṃ hiṃsyāc chīghram anāgasam
english: Even as I, guilt-laden, shall abandon this body through grief for a son, so may the elder son of Raibhya quickly slay that blameless man.

sanskrit: sukhino vai narā yeṣāṃ jātyā putro na vidyate te putraśokam aprāpya vicaranti yathāsukham
english: Truly happy are those men who by their very birth have no son — never reaching the grief of a son, they wander about at ease.

sanskrit: ye tu putrakṛtāc chokād bhṛśaṃ vyākulacetasaḥ śapantīṣṭān sakhīn ārtās tebhyaḥ pāpataro nu kaḥ
english: But those whose minds are deeply distraught by grief caused by a son, who in their anguish curse their beloved friends — who indeed is more sinful than they?

sanskrit: parāsuś ca suto dṛṣṭaḥ śaptaś ceṣṭaḥ sakhā mayā īdṛśīm āpadaṃ ko nu dvitīyo 'nubhaviṣyati
english: My son has been seen as lifeless, and my beloved friend has been cursed by me — who else in the world could experience such a calamity a second time?

sanskrit: vilapyaivaṃ bahuvidhaṃ bharadvājo 'dahat sutam susamiddhaṃ tataḥ paścāt praviveśa hutāśanam
english: Having lamented thus in many ways, Bharadvāja cremated his son with a well-kindled fire, and thereafter entered the flames himself.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca etasminn eva kāle tu bṛhaddyumno mahīpatiḥ satram āste mahābhāgo raibhyayājyaḥ pratāpavān
english: Lomaśa said: At this very time, the king Bṛhaddyumna, a man of great fortune and valor, the sacrificial patron of Raibhya, was performing a soma sacrifice.

sanskrit: tena raibhyasya vai putrāv arvāvasuparāvasū vṛtau sahāyau satrārthe bṛhaddyumnena dhīmatā
english: By that wise Bṛhaddyumna, Raibhya's two sons, Arvāvasu and Parāvasu, were invited as assistants for the purpose of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tatra tau samanujñātau pitrā kaunteya jagmatuḥ āśrame tv abhavad raibhyo bhāryā caiva parāvasoḥ
english: There, the two, having obtained their father's permission, O son of Kuntī, departed. In the hermitage, however, Raibhya remained, along with the wife of Parāvasu.

sanskrit: athāvalokako 'gacchad gṛhān ekaḥ parāvasuḥ kṛṣṇājinena saṃvītaṃ dadarśa pitaraṃ vane
english: Then Parāvasu went home alone to look in on things, and in the forest he saw his father wrapped in a black antelope skin.

sanskrit: jaghanyarātre nidrāndhaḥ sāvaśeṣe tamasy api carantaṃ gahane 'raṇye mene sa pitaraṃ mṛgam
english: In the dead of night, blinded by sleep, with some darkness still remaining, he saw him moving through the dense forest and mistook his father for a deer.

sanskrit: mṛgaṃ tu manyamānena pitā vai tena hiṃsitaḥ akāmayānena tadā śarīratrāṇam icchatā
english: Thinking him a deer, he then slew his father — not desiring to do so, only wishing to protect his own body.

sanskrit: sa tasya pretakāryāṇi kṛtvā sarvāṇi bhārata punar āgamya tat satram abravīd bhrātaraṃ vacaḥ
english: He performed all the funeral rites for him, O Bhārata, and returning again to that sacrifice, he spoke these words to his brother.

sanskrit: idaṃ karma na śaktas tvaṃ voḍhum ekaḥ kathaṃ cana mayā tu hiṃsitas tāto manyamānena taṃ mṛgam
english: "This deed you are in no way able to bear alone. I have slain father, mistaking him for a deer.

sanskrit: so 'smadarthe vrataṃ sādhu cara tvaṃ brahmahiṃsanam samartho hy aham ekākī karma kartum idaṃ mune
english: For our sake, duly observe the vow for brahmin-slaying; I am capable of performing this rite alone, O sage."

sanskrit: arvāvasur uvāca karotu vai bhavān satraṃ bṛhaddyumnasya dhīmataḥ brahmahatyāṃ cariṣye 'haṃ tvadarthaṃ niyatendriyaḥ
english: Arvāvasu said: "Let you carry out the sacrifice of the wise Bṛhaddyumna; I shall observe the penance for brahmin-slaying on your behalf, with my senses restrained."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca sa tasyā brahmahatyāyāḥ pāraṃ gatvā yudhiṣṭhira arvāvasus tadā satram ājagāma punar muniḥ
english: Lomaśa said: Having passed beyond that sin of brahmin-slaying, O Yudhiṣṭhira, Arvāvasu the sage then returned again to the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tataḥ parāvasur dṛṣṭvā bhrātaraṃ samupasthitam bṛhaddyumnam uvācedaṃ vacanaṃ pariṣadgatam
english: Then Parāvasu, seeing his brother arrive, spoke these words to Bṛhaddyumna in the assembly:

sanskrit: eṣa te brahmahā yajñaṃ mā draṣṭuṃ praviśed iti brahmahā prekṣitenāpi pīḍayet tvāṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: "This brahmin-killer should not be allowed to enter and witness your sacrifice; even the mere sight of a brahmin-killer would afflict you, there is no doubt."

sanskrit: preṣyair utsāryamāṇas tu rājann arvāvasus tadā na mayā brahmahatyeyaṃ kṛtety āha punaḥ punaḥ
english: Being driven away by the servants, O king, Arvāvasu then said again and again, "This brahmin-slaying was not done by me!"

sanskrit: ucyamāno 'sakṛt preṣyair brahmahann iti bhārata naiva sa pratijānāti brahmahatyāṃ svayaṃ kṛtām mama bhrātrā kṛtam idaṃ mayā tu parirakṣitam
english: Though called brahmin-killer again and again by the servants, O Bhārata, he would not at all acknowledge the brahmin-slaying as done by himself: "This was done by my brother; by me it was only borne to protect him."

sanskrit: prītās tasyābhavan devāḥ karmaṇārvāvasor nṛpa taṃ te pravarayām āsur nirāsuś ca parāvasum
english: The gods were pleased by Arvāvasu's deed, O king; they exalted him and expelled Parāvasu.

sanskrit: tato devā varaṃ tasmai dadur agnipurogamāḥ sa cāpi varayām āsa pitur utthānam ātmanaḥ
english: Then the gods, with Agni at their head, granted him a boon; and he in turn chose the resurrection of his father and his own exoneration.

sanskrit: anāgastvaṃ tathā bhrātuḥ pituś cāsmaraṇaṃ vadhe bharadvājasya cotthānaṃ yavakrītasya cobhayoḥ
english: Also the blamelessness of his brother, and the forgetting of the killing by his father, and the resurrection of Bharadvāja and of Yavakrīta — both of them.

sanskrit: tataḥ prādurbabhūvus te sarva eva yudhiṣṭhira athābravīd yavakrīto devān agnipurogamān
english: Then all of them appeared, O Yudhiṣṭhira. Thereupon Yavakrīta addressed the gods, with Agni at their head:

sanskrit: samadhītaṃ mayā brahma vratāni caritāni ca kathaṃ nu raibhyaḥ śakto mām adhīyānaṃ tapasvinam tathāyuktena vidhinā nihantum amarottamāḥ
english: "I have mastered the Veda and the vows have been observed by me — how then was Raibhya able to slay me, a student and ascetic, by such a method, O best among immortals?"

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ maivaṃ kṛthā yavakrīta yathā vadasi vai mune ṛte gurum adhītā hi sukhaṃ vedās tvayā purā
english: The gods said: "Do not do this, O Yavakrīta, as you speak, O sage! The Vedas were formerly studied by you easily, without a teacher.

sanskrit: anena tu gurūn duḥkhāt toṣayitvā svakarmaṇā kālena mahatā kleśād brahmādhigatam uttamam
english: But by this one — Arvāvasu — through great time and toil and by his own deeds, having pleased his teachers with difficulty, the highest Brahmā-knowledge was attained."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca yavakrītam athoktvaivaṃ devāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ saṃjīvayitvā tān sarvān punar jagmus triviṣṭapam
english: Lomaśa said: Having thus spoken to Yavakrīta, the gods with Agni at their head, having revived all of them, departed again to heaven.

sanskrit: āśramas tasya puṇyo 'yaṃ sadāpuṣpaphaladrumaḥ atroṣya rājaśārdūla sarvapāpaiḥ pramokṣyase
english: "This is that holy hermitage, always filled with flowering and fruit-bearing trees. Having dwelt here, O tiger among kings, you shall be released from all sins."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca uśīrabījaṃ mainākaṃ giriṃ śvetaṃ ca bhārata samatīto 'si kaunteya kālaśailaṃ ca pārthiva
english: Lomaśa said: You have passed beyond Uśīrabīja, the Maināka mountain, the White Mountain, O Bhārata, and Kālaśaila too, O king, O son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: eṣā gaṅgā saptavidhā rājate bharatarṣabha sthānaṃ virajasaṃ ramyaṃ yatrāgnir nityam idhyate
english: Here the Gaṅgā shines in her sevenfold form, O bull of the Bhāratas — a pure and lovely place where fire is constantly kindled.

sanskrit: etad vai mānuṣeṇādya na śakyaṃ draṣṭum apy uta samādhiṃ kurutāvyagrās tīrthāny etāni drakṣyatha
english: This indeed cannot ordinarily be seen even by a human being today — focus your minds with undivided attention, and you shall behold these sacred tīrthas.

sanskrit: śvetaṃ giriṃ pravekṣyāmo mandaraṃ caiva parvatam yatra māṇicaro yakṣaḥ kuberaś cāpi yakṣarāṭ
english: We shall enter the White Mountain and also Mount Mandara, where the yakṣa Māṇicara dwells, and Kubera, the king of yakṣas.

sanskrit: aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi gandharvāḥ śīghracāriṇaḥ tathā kiṃpuruṣā rājan yakṣāś caiva caturguṇāḥ
english: Eighty-eight thousand gandharvas who move with speed, and kiṃpuruṣas, O king, and yakṣas four times their number —

sanskrit: anekarūpasaṃsthānā nānāpraharaṇāś ca te yakṣendraṃ manujaśreṣṭha māṇibhadram upāsate
english: — of many forms and bearing various weapons, they attend upon Māṇibhadra, the lord of yakṣas, O best among men.

sanskrit: teṣām ṛddhir atīvāgryā gatau vāyusamāś ca te sthānāt pracyāvayeyur ye devarājam api dhruvam
english: Their prosperity is exceedingly great, and in movement they are equal to the wind — they could surely dislodge even the king of the gods from his position.

sanskrit: tais tāta balibhir guptā yātudhānaiś ca rakṣitāḥ durgamāḥ parvatāḥ pārtha samādhiṃ paramaṃ kuru
english: Protected by those mighty ones and guarded by the yātudhānas, these mountains are hard to approach, dear son; gather your highest concentration, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: kuberasacivāś cānye raudrā maitrāś ca rākṣasāḥ taiḥ sameṣyāma kaunteya yatto vikramaṇe bhava
english: There are also other rākṣasas, ministers of Kubera, both fierce and friendly — we shall encounter them, O son of Kuntī; be alert and ready for any advance.

sanskrit: kailāsaḥ parvato rājan ṣaḍyojanaśatāny uta yatra devāḥ samāyānti viśālā yatra bhārata
english: Mount Kailāsa extends for six hundred yojanas, O king; it is vast, O Bhārata, and there the gods assemble.

sanskrit: asaṃkhyeyās tu kaunteya yakṣarākṣasakiṃnarāḥ nāgāḥ suparṇā gandharvāḥ kuberasadanaṃ prati
english: Countless yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kiṃnaras, O son of Kuntī, as well as nāgas, suparṇas, and gandharvas — all approach the abode of Kubera.

sanskrit: tān vigāhasva pārthādya tapasā ca damena ca rakṣyamāṇo mayā rājan bhīmasenabalena ca
english: Plunge among them today, O Pārtha, with asceticism and self-restraint, protected by me, O king, and by the strength of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: svasti te varuṇo rājā yamaś ca samitiṃjayaḥ gaṅgā ca yamunā caiva parvataś ca dadhātu te
english: May King Varuṇa and Yama the conqueror of battles, and the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, and the mountains grant you well-being.

sanskrit: indrasya jāmbūnadaparvatāgre; śṛṇomi ghoṣaṃ tava devi gaṅge gopāyayemaṃ subhage giribhyaḥ; sarvājamīḍhāpacitaṃ narendram bhavasva śarma pravivikṣato 'sya; śailān imāñ śailasute nṛpasya
english: "At the summit of Indra's golden Jāmbūnada mountain, I hear your voice, O goddess Gaṅgā — protect this auspicious one from these mountains. Be a shelter for this king, descendant of all the Ajamīḍhas, who is about to enter these peaks, O daughter of the mountain."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca apūrvo 'yaṃ saṃbhramo lomaśasya; kṛṣṇāṃ sarve rakṣata mā pramādam deśo hy ayaṃ durgatamo mato 'sya; tasmāt paraṃ śaucam ihācaradhvam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "This agitation of Lomaśa is unprecedented. All of you, guard Kṛṣṇā — be not careless! This region is considered by him to be extremely perilous. Therefore observe the highest purity here."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'bravīd bhīmam udāravīryaṃ; kṛṣṇāṃ yattaḥ pālaya bhīmasena śūnye 'rjune 'saṃnihite ca tāta; tvam eva kṛṣṇāṃ bhajase 'sukheṣu
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then he spoke to Bhīma of noble valor: "Guard Kṛṣṇā vigilantly, O Bhīmasena. When Arjuna is absent and not present, dear son, it is you alone who are devoted to Kṛṣṇā in times of hardship."

sanskrit: tato mahātmā yamajau sametya; mūrdhany upāghrāya vimṛjya gātre uvāca tau bāṣpakalaṃ sa rājā; mā bhaiṣṭam āgacchatam apramattau
english: Then the great-souled king, gathering the twin sons of Yama to himself, smelling their heads and stroking their limbs, spoke to them with tears in his voice: "Do not be afraid; come, both of you, and be vigilant."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca antarhitāni bhūtāni rakṣāṃsi balavanti ca agninā tapasā caiva śakyaṃ gantuṃ vṛkodara
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "The creatures that have vanished and the powerful rākṣasas — it is only by fire and by asceticism that one can pass through, O Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: saṃnivartaya kaunteya kṣutpipāse balānvayāt tato balaṃ ca dākṣyaṃ ca saṃśrayasva kurūdvaha
english: Restrain hunger and thirst, O son of Kuntī, as befits your strength; then take recourse to strength and skill, O foremost of the Kurus.

sanskrit: ṛṣes tvayā śrutaṃ vākyaṃ kailāsaṃ parvataṃ prati buddhyā prapaśya kaunteya kathaṃ kṛṣṇā gamiṣyati
english: You have heard the sage's words regarding Mount Kailāsa — consider carefully in your mind, O son of Kuntī, how Kṛṣṇā is to make the journey.

sanskrit: atha vā sahadevena dhaumyena ca sahābhibho sūdaiḥ paurogavaiś caiva sarvaiś ca paricārakaiḥ
english: Or else, O splendid one, with Sahadeva, with Dhaumya, together with the cooks and the chief stewards and all the attendants —

sanskrit: rathair aśvaiś ca ye cānye viprāḥ kleśāsahāḥ pathi sarvais tvaṃ sahito bhīma nivartasvāyatekṣaṇa
english: — with chariots and horses, and those other brahmins who cannot endure hardship on the road — together with all of them, turn back, O Bhīma, O broad-eyed one.

sanskrit: trayo vayaṃ gamiṣyāmo laghvāhārā yatavratāḥ ahaṃ ca nakulaś caiva lomaśaś ca mahātapāḥ
english: Three of us shall go, eating lightly, with vows observed: I, and Nakula, and Lomaśa of great austerity.

sanskrit: mamāgamanam ākāṅkṣan gaṅgādvāre samāhitaḥ vaseha draupadīṃ rakṣan yāvadāgamanaṃ mama
english: Awaiting my return, dwell here at Gaṅgādvāra in a collected state of mind, guarding Draupadī, until I come back."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca rājaputrī śrameṇārtā duḥkhārtā caiva bhārata vrajaty eva hi kalyāṇī śvetavāhadidṛkṣayā
english: Bhīma said: "The princess, though afflicted by fatigue and overcome with suffering, O Bhārata, presses on nonetheless — that gracious one, eager to see the White-Horsed one.

sanskrit: tava cāpy aratis tīvrā vardhate tam apaśyataḥ kiṃ punaḥ sahadevaṃ ca māṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃ ca bhārata
english: And your own intense yearning grows as you do not see him — how much more so for Sahadeva, for me, and for Kṛṣṇā, O Bhārata?

sanskrit: rathāḥ kāmaṃ nivartantāṃ sarve ca paricārakāḥ sūdāḥ paurogavāś caiva manyate yatra no bhavān
english: Let the chariots turn back, willingly, and all the attendants, the cooks and the chief stewards — wherever you think best for us.

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ hātum icchāmi bhavantam iha karhi cit śaile 'smin rākṣasākīrṇe durgeṣu viṣameṣu ca
english: For I do not wish to leave you here at any time, in these mountains swarming with rākṣasas, in these difficult and treacherous places.

sanskrit: iyaṃ cāpi mahābhāgā rājaputrī yatavratā tvām ṛte puruṣavyāghra notsahed vinivartitum
english: And this great-fortuned princess who keeps her vows — without you, O tiger among men, she would not venture to turn back.

sanskrit: tathaiva sahadevo 'yaṃ satataṃ tvām anuvrataḥ na jātu vinivarteta matajño hy aham asya vai
english: Likewise this Sahadeva, ever devoted to you in vow, would never turn back — of this I am the knower of his mind.

sanskrit: api cātra mahārāja savyasācididṛkṣayā sarve lālasabhūtāḥ sma tasmād yāsyāmahe saha
english: Furthermore here, O great king, we are all filled with longing to see Savyasācī — therefore we shall go together.

sanskrit: yady aśakyo rathair gantuṃ śailo 'yaṃ bahukandaraḥ padbhir eva gamiṣyāmo mā rājan vimanā bhava
english: If this mountain with its many ravines cannot be traversed by chariots, we shall go on foot — do not be disheartened, O king.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vahiṣye pāñcālīṃ yatra yatra na śakṣyati iti me vartate buddhir mā rājan vimanā bhava
english: I shall carry the Pāñcālī wherever she cannot manage — this is the resolve in my mind; do not be disheartened, O king.

sanskrit: sukumārau tathā vīrau mādrīnandikarāv ubhau durge saṃtārayiṣyāmi yady aśaktau bhaviṣyataḥ
english: And those two tender heroes, the twin joys of Mādrī — if they are unable, I shall carry both of them through the difficult passages."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca evaṃ te bhāṣamāṇasya balaṃ bhīmābhivardhatām yas tvam utsahase voḍhuṃ draupadīṃ vipule 'dhvani
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Even as you speak thus, may your strength grow ever greater, O Bhīma — you who undertake to carry Draupadī on the vast road.

sanskrit: yamajau cāpi bhadraṃ te naitad anyatra vidyate balaṃ ca te yaśaś caiva dharmaḥ kīrtiś ca vardhatām
english: And blessings on you for the twin sons of Yama as well — such as this is found nowhere else. May your strength and your fame, your righteousness and your glory all increase.

sanskrit: yas tvam utsahase netuṃ bhrātarau saha kṛṣṇayā mā te glānir mahābāho mā ca te 'stu parābhavaḥ
english: You who undertake to lead both brothers together with Kṛṣṇā — may you feel no weariness, O great-armed one, and may no defeat be yours."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kṛṣṇābravīd vākyaṃ prahasantī manoramā gamiṣyāmi na saṃtāpaḥ kāryo māṃ prati bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Kṛṣṇā, the lovely one, laughing gently, spoke these words: "I shall go — no distress need be felt on my account, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tapasā śakyate gantuṃ parvato gandhamādanaḥ tapasā caiva kaunteya sarve yokṣyāmahe vayam
english: Lomaśa said: "Mount Gandhamādana can only be reached through ascetic power; and through that ascetic power, O son of Kuntī, we shall all gird ourselves.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca bhīmasenaś ca pārthiva ahaṃ ca tvaṃ ca kaunteya drakṣyāmaḥ śvetavāhanam
english: Nakula and Sahadeva, and Bhīmasena, O king, and I, and you, O son of Kuntī — we shall behold the White-Horsed one."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇās te subāhor viṣayaṃ mahat dadṛśur muditā rājan prabhūtagajavājimat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Conversing thus, they came joyfully to the great domain of Subāhu, O king, teeming with abundant elephants and horses.

sanskrit: kirātataṅgaṇākīrṇaṃ kuṇindaśatasaṃkulam himavaty amarair juṣṭaṃ bahvāścaryasamākulam
english: Filled with Kirātas and Taṅgaṇas, thronged with hundreds of Kuṇindas, frequented by immortals on the Himālayas, and crowded with many wonders.

sanskrit: subāhuś cāpi tān dṛṣṭvā pūjayā pratyagṛhṇata viṣayānte kuṇindānām īśvaraḥ prītipūrvakam
english: And Subāhu, the lord of the Kuṇindas, seeing them at the boundary of his territory, received them with honor and with affection.

sanskrit: tatra te pūjitās tena sarva eva sukhoṣitāḥ pratasthur vimale sūrye himavantaṃ giriṃ prati
english: There, honored by him and having dwelt comfortably, all of them set out toward the Himālaya mountain under a clear sun.

sanskrit: indrasenamukhāṃś caiva bhṛtyān paurogavāṃs tathā sūdāṃś ca paribarhaṃ ca draupadyāḥ sarvaśo nṛpa
english: Handing over to them the servants headed by Indrasena, the chief stewards, the cooks, and all the retinue of Draupadī, O king —

sanskrit: rājñaḥ kuṇindādhipateḥ paridāya mahārathāḥ padbhir eva mahāvīryā yayuḥ kauravanandanāḥ
english: — entrusting them to the king, the lord of the Kuṇindas, those great warriors, the joyful sons of the Kurus, of mighty valor, proceeded on foot.

sanskrit: te śanaiḥ prādravan sarve kṛṣṇayā saha pāṇḍavāḥ tasmād deśāt susaṃhṛṣṭā draṣṭukāmā dhanaṃjayam
english: All those Pāṇḍavas, together with Kṛṣṇā, departed slowly from that region, overjoyed, longing to see Dhanañjaya.
